It may partly derive from the arm lyra and the Byzantine lyre. In the Renaissance the bow gradually took the straight modern form, and makers also accepted a gourd-shaped outline. In the Classical period the violin became dominant and the four instruments were standardised, forming the orchestra and the string quartet. The cello developed from the bass violin, and the origin of the double bass is disputed, though historically it has taken the lowest part; an octave double bass appeared in the nineteenth century. In modern times the family reached East Asia from Europe; the Chinese word 提琴 refers mainly to it, and on entering China it changed considerably, developing into the huqin.

A standard string quartet is two violins, a viola and a cello, and a string quintet adds another viola or cello, with a double bass when needed. They are also used, less often, in jazz, electronic music, rock and other popular music, often amplified or in the form of electric violins; an electric violin can be turned down for evening practice. The violin also appears in fiddle music, country music and folk music, and the double bass is important in both classical music and jazz. The octave double bass occasionally appears in Romantic scores and modern works.

The violin family is a group of wooden bowed string instruments that developed in Italy in Europe; by sound production they are chordophones, Hornbostel–Sachs number 321.322-71. The standard modern members are the violin, viola and cello, with the double bass often counted as the lowest member. Each instrument has a neck and a bow, carries four strings, and is mainly bowed, though it can also be plucked with the fingers; the violin and viola are held under the chin, the cello is played seated between the knees, and the double bass is played standing or on a stool. The violin family is used in classical music, orchestras and string quartets, and also appears in jazz, electronic music, rock, pop, country and folk music.
提琴族為弦鳴樂器，基本操作是先以一手持琴杆、另一手持琴弓，琴身通常張四根弦，以弓: The violin family belongs to the chordophones. The basic routine is to hold the neck with one hand and the bow with the other; the body carries four strings, and the instrument is mostly bowed, though it can also be plucked with the fingers. The violin and viola are played under the chin; the cello is played seated with the body between the knees; the double bass is played standing or on a stool. A beginner can check hold, bow grip and bowed or plucked stroke in that order.
提琴族為木製弓弦樂器，以琴弓摩擦弦發聲，也可用手指撥奏。各器音域重疊，音色差異主: The violin family consists of wooden bowed instruments: the bow rubs the strings, and the fingers can also pluck them. The ranges overlap, and the difference in timbre comes mainly from size and register: the violin and viola are held under the chin, the violin from G3 to E7 and up to A7, the viola from C3 to A6, a fifth lower than the violin. The cello is played between the knees, from C2 to A5, an octave below the viola. The double bass is played standing or on a stool, from E1 to C5, and with a mechanical extension or a fifth string down to C1/B0, six, eight or nine tones below the cello. The sources give no details of volume control.

The belly is mostly spruce, thinner at the edges and thicker in the middle; the back is mostly maple, with some Baroque instruments using poplar or willow. Neck, bridge and ribs are maple, and the nut is often ebony. The materials of the remaining parts are not recorded.
